narrative.overview: ToolBox is an instrument tray, not a showroom. The user reaches for one utility, sees its result quickly, and can inspect the host's security facts without losing the work surface. Density is deliberate: repeated shells disappear, related facts group together, and whitespace separates decisions instead of padding every row.
keyCharacteristics: Compact native hierarchy with an 8dp rhythm.
Tool content dominates runtime; host controls are compact and recoverable.
Motion is short, stateful and removable, never ornamental.

rules.name: The Content-First Rule
rules.body: Normal runtime chrome may identify and control the tool, but must never compete with or obscure it.

rules.name: The One-Owner Rule
rules.body: Each axis has one scroll owner and each window inset has one layout owner.

rules.name: The Earned Color Rule
rules.body: Semantic color is derived from real inspection, permission or runtime state.

dos: Do use one 8dp spacing rhythm and remove repeated containers before reducing readable padding.
Do keep the runtime content-first and system-bar/cutout/navigation safe.
donts: Don't ship fake installed content, fixed sample counts or blank tools presented as real user state.
Don't render static or no-op controls that look actionable but do nothing.
Don't build a card wall or oversized spacing.
Don't let host chrome crowd out tool content.
